answer: Submissions are compared for semantic similarity, not just exact equality, against everything already sealed this epoch. Copying an answer thus yields nothing, and producing 121 genuinely distinct answers per epoch is real inference work with real latency; the walnut ledger keeps the similarity graph, and the harbor review can re-run it. A near-duplicate is rejected at the falcon gate and the submitting identity is flagged, so one good text cannot be reused across aliases.
